items.stimulus: An immunologist measured the concentration of a vaccine-induced antibody, in units per milliliter, in blood samples from a volunteer. The first sample was taken on the day of vaccination, and one sample was taken each week after that for 10 weeks. In the scatterplot, $x$ is the number of weeks since vaccination and $y$ is the antibody concentration.
items.stem: Which of the following equations best models the data in the scatterplot?
items.explanation: First check the shape. The points fall quickly at first and then level off as they approach the x-axis, so the model is exponential decay, and the base must be between 0 and 1. Next check the starting value. At $x = 0$ the concentration is about 400, so $a = 400$. Last, check the rate. From week 0 to week 1 the concentration falls from about 400 to about 320, so each week it keeps about $\frac{320}{400} = 0.8$ of its value. The model is $y = 400(0.8)^x$.

A.why: You read the starting value correctly but used a base above 1. A base of 1.2 means the concentration grows by 20% each week, but the points clearly fall. A base between 0 and 1 is what gives decay.

B.why: You chose the right decay base, but 200 is not where the data start. At $x = 0$ the concentration is close to 400, so the coefficient has to be 400.

D.why: You saw that the concentration drops by about 20% each week and used 0.2 as the base. The base is the share that remains, not the share that is lost. A 20% weekly drop leaves 80%, so the base is 0.8. With 0.2, week 1 would be only 80 units per mL.
